CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY KUMAR SINGH  ORAL ORDER 6 06-01-2026 1-Heard learned counsel for the appellant, learned Additional Public Prosecutor representing the State.

2-This appeal under Sections 14A(1) of the SC/ST POA Act, 1989 read with Section 415 (2) and 438(1) of B.N.S.S. has been preferred by the appellant namely Kamlesh Kumar Mahto against the judgment of conviction dated 22.11.2024 and order of sentence dated 02.12.2024 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (POA) in Case No 476 of 2013 arising out of Bahera Police Station Case No.
333 of 2012, under Section 366 of Indian Penal Code, District Darbhanga, convicting and sentencing the appellant for five years' rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 5,000/- (Five Thousand) for the offence under Section 366 and in default of payment of fine, three months additional imprisonment.

Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.39 of 2025(6) dt.06-01-2026 3-The appellant has prayed for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal before this Court.

entities.text: High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.39 of 2025(6)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4-Brief facts of the case, which are required to be stated are that the complainant who is grandfather of victim got a First Information Report lodged against the appellant Kamlesh Kumar Mahto alleging inter alia that the accused-appellant, who runs a grocery shop next to his house, trapped his granddaughter in his love and kidnapped her on 19.08.2012 at about 11:00 p.m. by luring her with the promise of performing marriage.
F.I.R. further alleges that he is confident that his minor granddaughter will be raped or taken to some other place.
He searched a lot on his own, but she could not be found.
5-It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant is innocent and due to personal enmity with the family members of the victim, he has falsely been implicated in this case.

1 judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the appellant is not sustainable in the eyes of the law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that initially FIR was lodged for the offences under Sections 364, 366A and 370 of the Indian Penal Code.

Charges were framed against the appellant for the offence under Section 366, 366A, 376 of the IPC and Section 3(i)(x), 3(2)(v) Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.39 of 2025(6) dt.06-01-2026 SC/ST POA Act but after completing the trial, appellant has been convicted only for the offence under Section 366 of the Indian Penal Code.

Referring the statement of Doctor, it is also pointed out that on the basis of physical and radiological findings of victim,
doctor has opined that the victim was aged between 16 to 17 years and there was no evidence to suggest commission of recent sexual intercourse with her.
Hence the prosecution case is not corroborated from the medical evidence of the victim.
Much emphasis has been given by contending that there are material contradictions in the statement of prosecution witnesses.
Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the appellant have also been placed forth before the Court.

Lastly, it is submitted that in case appellant is granted bail,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in early hearing of this appeal.

6-Learned A.P.P. for the State opposed the prayer for bail by contending that prosecution has proved it's case beyond reasonable doubt, hence at this stage presumption of innocence is not available to the appellant.

7-Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in it's entirety, I find that trial Court has recorded specific finding that victim in her statement under Patna High Court CR.
APP (SJ) No.39 of 2025(6) dt.06-01-2026 Section 164 Cr.P.C. did not make allegation of committing any misdeed against the appellant, which is also corroborated from the medical report of the victim.
The trial Court has acquitted the appellant of the charge under Section 375 I.P.C., as such part of the prosecution allegation has been disbelieved by the trial Court.
As per own statement of the victim recorded before the trial Court, appellant used to lure her to marry.
She left her house on 19.08.2012 at about 11:00 O'clock and had gone with the appellant, who took her to Sakri in a tempo.
Victim while going with the appellant was comfortable and did not raise alarm, though she had an ample opportunity to do so.

Radiological age of the victim was found between 16 to 17 years,
hence she was capable to understand the significance and morality associated with the act, for which she was consenting to.
Investigating Officer of this case was also not produced by the prosecution.
The appellant has been convicted under Section 366 of Indian Penal Code only.
The maximum sentence for the alleged offence awarded to the appellant is up to five years, against which he has served one year four months.
Considering the huge pendency of the cases, appeal is not likely to be heard before completing the entire sentence.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in more or less similar matter in the case of Tilku alias Tilak Patna High Court CR.

sentences.text: , this Court without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case is of the view that the appellant is liable to be released on bail during pendency of this Criminal Appeal.
9-The sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this Criminal Appeal.

10-Let the appellant- Kamlesh Kumar Mahto be enlarged on bail during pendency of this appeal in above Case on his furnishing bail bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned.

The realization of Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.39 of 2025(6)
dt.06-01-2026 amount of fine shall remain stayed till disposal of this Criminal Appeal.
11-On acceptance of bail bonds, the concerned Court below shall furnish the photocopy thereof to this Court for being kept on record of this Criminal Appeal.
12-Let this Criminal Appeal be listed in due course for hearing.

(Sanjay Kumar Singh , J) Raj Ranjan/-
